category_title: Adolescents with ADHD exhibiting low levels of agency, chronic procrastination, and disorganized academic behaviors
scenario_title: Managing a long-term research project and overcoming procrastination
minimal_context: The student is sitting down to work on a four-page research assignment the day before it is due.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Let's look at your four-page research assignment. You have the instruction sheet and rubric here, and it needs to be completed.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I started thinking about it pretty much right away when we got the sheet, but I haven't done the actual work. I guess I'm just lazy when it comes to tasks that take sustained mental effort.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: What are some ways you might improve your progress on this assignment?

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I mean, if I could just be more organized and do not procrastinate... Like, I just... like, I'll sit home... I've got, like, a four-page thing due in two days and I say I'm going to get it done, then next thing I know, it's 12:00 the day before and I don't have it done yet.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Well, it is due tomorrow. Go ahead and start writing the four pages now.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I can't, I'm completely daunted by the scope of this project! I started freaking out because it's 4 a.m., and it's due the next day, and I have no idea what I wrote... 'cause it's so late... so I burst out into tears and I ran downstairs and I was, like, crying to my mom.
